A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present study demonstrates the feasibility to optimize the performance of GFP-based redox probes by extending the linker and exchanging the FRET pair.
we report a novel redox probe with a significantly improved FRET dynamic range, which is based on the optimized RL7 linker and the mCyPet/mYPet FRET pair.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of redox-sensitive FRET probes can be optimized by careful selection of the α-helix-based linker, which is the main determinant of FRET signal strength, and by using monomeric variants of FRET donor and/or acceptor fluorescent proteins to eliminate dimerization artifacts.
a combination of a longer linker sequence with a more oxidizing midpoint redox potential can be used to improve FRET-based redox sensors.

it is possible to design and optimize a redox sensor with an improved dynamic range and an oxidative midpoint potential in the physiological redox range, which can be used to monitor redox changes in the cytosol and other subcellular compartments.
